sentences.text: This animal is distinguished by large eyelids fused to the skull bones and a mix of different tooth shapes.
Its teeth include at least four distinct types: pseudocaniniforms, two types of lanceolate teeth, and low-crowned teeth.
A unique feature is the W-shaped overlap between its nasal and prefrontal bones, distinguishing it from Sabresuchus.
Fossils were discovered in the Pui Gater locality within the Hateg Basin of modern-day Transylvania, Romania.
The genus is known from an incomplete skull and mandibles, the holotype, and a cervical vertebra found nearby.
The name Aprosuchus combines the Hungarian word for 'small' and the Ancient Greek word for 'crocodile'.
The species name ghirai was chosen to honor Ioan Ghira of Babeș-Bolyai University for his work in herpetology.
The genus was described by Venczel and Codrea in 2019.
Researchers suggest that the small Aprosuchus likely fed on invertebrates and small vertebrates.
The existence of Aprosuchus indicates that atoposaurid lineages survived into the Late Cretaceous by inhabiting island ecosystems in the Eastern Tethys.
Aprosuchus belongs to the family Atoposauridae.
It is classified as a reptile.
Phylogenetic analysis places Aprosuchus closely related to other atoposaurids, distinct from Wannchampsus and the Glen Rose Form.
Aprosuchus was a small-bodied crocodile relative that lived during the Maastrichtian stage in the Hateg Basin of Romania.
It lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
The variety of tooth shapes in Aprosuchus raises questions about using teeth alone to identify atoposaurid genera beyond the family level.
